ops.statement: In a multi-ship/fleet session, NEVER broad-kill processes (e.g. `taskkill //IM python.exe`) — it kills sibling ships' compute. Kill by explicit PID, and check `ps -W` start-time/ownership before any sweep; treat clustered same-timestamp processes you didn't launch as a sibling's.
ops.grounding: .agent-work/staged-feedback/638-f12-stability-rework/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md 2026-07-18 (Where I improvised): I ran `taskkill //IM python.exe` to clear a stray diagnostic, which in a multi-ship session could have killed sibling ships' compute; corrected to surgical `kill <pid>` after checking ps timestamps (7 clustered sibling procs were spared on the next sweep).
ops.bank_reason: Re-observe whether surgical-PID discipline holds under fleet contention, and whether a shared convention (ship-tagged process names / a ps-ownership helper) is needed to make orphan-sweeping safe — a single incident doesn't yet prove the general mechanism.
